title: Tiefgang – an underwater roguelite co-op FPS built mostly by autonomous AI agents (Godot 4) – gameplay video
author: Substantial-Mix-3772
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev!

I'm a solo dev, and for the past few weeks I've been building **Tiefgang**, a roguelite co-op FPS set in sunken underwater temples. Most of the code was written by autonomous AI coding agents working from a single master spec.

🎥 Gameplay video: [https://youtu.be/mLpezN56qNA](https://youtu.be/mLpezN56qNA)  
🎮 Play it free: [https://osugerman.itch.io/tiefgang](https://osugerman.itch.io/tiefgang)

**My workflow:**  
**Code:** AI agents working autonomously in Godot 4 / GDScript, guided by a detailed SPEC.md plus an agent rules file (progress tracking, task list, capped testing time so they keep coding instead of over-testing)  
**Concept art:** Higgsfield  
**3D models:** Meshy (image-to-3D) → Blender MCP for cleanup, rigging and LODs → .glb into Godot  
**Me:** design, direction, playtesting and fixing what the agents get wrong

Happy to answer questions about the setup. And I'd love feedback on the game itself: what still screams "AI-made", and where does it hold up?

comments.author: TheCelestialBubble
comments.body:
I don't really love these posts. Ppl make a single doc, get agents to do everything, and then have the nerve to get reddit to do exactly what they should be doing as a 'game designer', which is actually critique it. A single doc is not even the bare minimum...

For your question though, I could not imagine paying any money for this, but I'm in general a fan of the genre. Firstly, the models are virtually static. Secondly, the game looks boring, all s/he does is shoot and occasionally ground pound? Where's the depth? The trailer could be cut from 55 to 10s, it just shows exactly the same thing over and over again. Idk what the game is other than shoot.

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: I wont play your game if you do not even have the decency to, at the very least, write your own sales pitch. Is the game as lazy as this reddit post? Probably.

comments.author: superstarblast
comments.body: I want to hear more about how you orchestrate the agents and keep them working re: worktrees, branches etc especially on features that have depenendencies on other features

comments.author: blueeetherabbit
comments.body:
